source_basis: NCCP 00823 v2 pages 1–4 and EMA Tepmetko product information updated 08/10/2026, sections 4.2–4.6, 4.8 and patient leaflet. Independent review remains pending.

risks.label: Lung inflammation / pneumonitis
risks.detail: ILD can be serious or fatal. New or worsening breathlessness, cough or fever needs urgent assessment. Suspected disease requires a hold; confirmed disease of any grade requires permanent stopping.

risks.label: Liver-test changes and liver injury
risks.detail: Blood tests may change before symptoms appear. Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or abdominal pain; important changes can require a hold, dose change or permanent stopping after assessment.

risks.label: Heart-rhythm changes
risks.detail: QTc prolongation can occur. Report palpitations, fainting or collapse; ECG, electrolyte and interacting-medicine review are used when clinically indicated.

risks.label: Swelling and fluid retention
risks.detail: Swelling is common and may affect movement, comfort or breathing. Report increasing swelling or sudden weight gain; treatment may require supportive care, a pause or dose change.

risks.label: Nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting
risks.detail: Report early and follow the agreed symptom plan. Severe diarrhoea, repeated vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent advice because dehydration can occur.

risks.label: Kidney and other blood-test changes
risks.detail: Creatinine, albumin and other blood tests can change. A creatinine rise may reflect altered handling of creatinine or true kidney impairment; it requires assessment rather than assumption.

risks.label: Pregnancy, contraception, fertility and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose; women using hormonal contraception should also use a barrier method. Men with a partner who could become pregnant should use barrier contraception for the same period. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least one week afterwards. Human fertility effects are not known; discuss fertility before starting.

risks.label: Medicine interactions
risks.detail: Ask the pharmacist to check all prescribed medicines, non-prescription medicines and supplements before changes. Tepotinib can affect medicines including dabigatran, digoxin, rosuvastatin and metformin. Supportive medicines may also affect heart rhythm; individual advice is needed.
